samples.question: A 5 by 5 square grid of cells stands on a white card.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the grid a small key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole grid by this rule: for every cell, count how many of its eight surrounding neighbours (the cells that touch it along an edge or at a corner) are dark; in the next round that cell is dark if and only if the count is exactly two, otherwise it is pale.  Note that a dark cell may turn pale and a pale cell may turn dark.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting grid of the next round.  After the last round, count how many cells in the 5 by 5 grid are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.
